def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagr.physical_scope: The symmetry vocabulary of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: symmetry data as triples (tau, xi, B) satisfying the model's Noether identity for the mechanical Lagrangian K - U, strict data and their exact relation to the chart-level infinitesimal point symmetries, the charge M v . xi - (K+U) tau - B together with its dimension and its behaviour under rescaling of the family parameter, and the status of the notion. The item defines only; it asserts no conservation law, no existence of any symmetry of a given model, and no empirical content.

def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagr:
## Definition

Adopt one force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: $N\ge1$ particle
labels with fixed masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ (clause (i)), an open
nondegenerate time window $I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$, an open configuration
domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ and a force map $F$ with the standing
continuity and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses of clause (iii) of that
postulate, and fix one inertial frame with adapted coordinates $(t,x)$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]). Adopt in addition a potential presentation
$(U,d)$ of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]: a function
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$ of dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ with $F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)+d_{i}(t,x,v)$,
with residual forces $d=(d_{1},\dots,d_{N})$ of the standing regularity. Let
$L=K-U$, $O:=I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ and $\mathsf M$ be the
mechanical Lagrangian, the chart domain and the mass operator of
[[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], so that $L$ is of class $C^{2}$
on the open set $O$ and $(O,L)$ is a time-dependent Lagrangian chart over
every $[a,b]\times Q$ with $[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$
([[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]]). Dimensions are read by
[[def-cm01-units]], inner products and norms are Euclidean
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. For a $C^{1}$ function
$\varphi$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ and
$(t,x,v)\in O$ write

$$D_{t}\varphi(t,x,v):=\varphi_{t}(t,x)+\varphi_{x}(t,x)\cdot v,$$

the derivative of $s\mapsto\varphi(s,x+v(s-t))$ at $s=t$; the last two slots
of $L$ are $(x,v)$, and $L_{t}$, $L_{x}$, $L_{v}$ are the gradients of $L$ in
its three slots ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]],
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]).

**(a) Symmetry datum.** A **symmetry datum of the model's mechanical
Lagrangian** is a triple $(\tau,\xi,B)$ of maps

$$\tau:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R,\qquad \xi:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad B:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R,$$

of class $C^{2}$, that satisfies for every $(t,x,v)\in O$ the **Noether
identity of the model**:

$$L_{t}(t,x,v)\,\tau(t,x)+L_{x}(t,x,v)\cdot\xi(t,x)+L_{v}(t,x,v)\cdot\bigl(D_{t}\xi(t,x,v)-v\,D_{t}\tau(t,x,v)\bigr)+L(t,x,v)\,D_{t}\tau(t,x,v)=D_{t}B(t,x,v).$$

Because $K(v)=\tfrac12 v\cdot\mathsf M v$ does not depend on $t$ or $x$ and
$U$ does not depend on $v$, the identity is the following identity among the
model's data:

$$-U_{t}(t,x)\tau(t,x)-\nabla_{x}U(t,x)\cdot\xi(t,x)+\bigl(\mathsf M v\bigr)\cdot\bigl(D_{t}\xi(t,x,v)-v\,D_{t}\tau(t,x,v)\bigr)+\bigl(K(v)-U(t,x)\bigr)D_{t}\tau(t,x,v)=D_{t}B(t,x,v).$$

It involves the declared potential $U$, the masses through $\mathsf M$, and
the boundary function $B$; it is an identity imposed on the model's declared
data on the whole state domain $O$.

**(b) Strict data and point symmetries.** A symmetry datum is **strict**
when $\tau\equiv0$; its identity reads
$L_{x}\cdot\xi+L_{v}\cdot D_{t}\xi=D_{t}B$. If a strict datum has $\xi$
independent of $t$, then the pair $(\xi,B)$ is an **infinitesimal point
symmetry of the chart $(O,L)$** in the sense of
[[def-cm-infinitesimal-point-symmetry]]: that definition's identity,
instantiated with $n=3N$ in the configuration slot, is verbatim
$L_{x}(t,x,v)\cdot\xi(x)+L_{v}(t,x,v)\cdot D\xi(x)v=B_{t}(t,x)+B_{x}(t,x)\cdot v$.
Conversely every infinitesimal point symmetry of the chart $(O,L)$ whose
boundary function is defined on $I_{0}\times Q$ is a strict datum with $\xi$
independent of $t$. A general datum is a **point symmetry with time
reparametrisation**: the family

$$x_{i}\longmapsto x_{i}+s\,\xi_{i}(t,x),\qquad t\longmapsto t+s\,\tau(t,x)$$

changes the coordinate velocity to first order by $D_{t}\xi-v\,D_{t}\tau$, and
the identity says that the infinitesimal variation of $L$ along the family is
the total time derivative $D_{t}B$ of the chart function $B$.

**(c) Charge.** The **charge of the datum** is the function

$$C:O\to\mathbb R,\qquad C(t,x,v):=L_{v}(t,x,v)\cdot\xi(t,x)-E(t,x,v)\,\tau(t,x)-B(t,x),$$

where

$$E(t,x,v):=L_{v}(t,x,v)\cdot v-L(t,x,v)=K(v)+U(t,x)$$

is the **mechanical energy function of the chart**
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]). Since $L_{v}=\mathsf M v$,

$$C(t,x,v)=\bigl(\mathsf M v\bigr)\cdot\xi(t,x)-\bigl(K(v)+U(t,x)\bigr)\tau(t,x)-B(t,x).$$

**(d) Dimensions and rescaling.** Read the family parameter $s$ as carrying a
declared unit $\sigma$ (for instance radians for a rotation family, seconds
for a time-reparametrisation family, or a dimensionless parameter). Then
$\tau$ has dimension $\tau\sigma^{-1}$, every component
$\xi_{i}$ has dimension $\ell\sigma^{-1}$, $B$ has dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}\sigma^{-1}$ (action per parameter unit) and
$C$ has the same dimension as $B$
([[def-cm01-units]]). Replacing $(\tau,\xi,B)$ by $(c\tau,c\xi,cB)$ with
a real constant $c\ne0$ — the same family reparametrised by $s\mapsto cs$ —
rescales $C$ by $c$.

**(e) Status.** This item fixes the model's symmetry vocabulary: which data
satisfy the model's Noether identity, and which function is their charge. It
asserts neither that a given model admits a nonzero symmetry datum, nor that
the charge of a datum is conserved. Conservation is proved under explicit
hypotheses by the theorems of this page, and the hypotheses must be verified
against the declared potential $U$ and the masses: a change of inertial frame,
the affine structure of the spacetime of [[post-cm01-spacetime]], or a
relabelling of the particle labels is a kinematic or descriptive operation and
is not by itself a symmetry datum of $L$. Every statement that uses a charge
names the potential representative used
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (c)); the effect of
changing the representative is recorded in the general Noether theorem of this
page.

pthm-cm08-point-noether.physical_scope: The point Noether theorem of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: for a strict symmetry datum of the mechanical Lagrangian that is independent of time, the charge M x' . xi - B is constant along every motion of the global potential branch; for an arbitrary presentation the charge of a strict datum has derivative equal to the residual force paired with the generator, so conservation holds exactly when that pairing vanishes along the motion. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared presentation, the symmetry identity and, in the conservation clause, on the absence of residual forces; it asserts no symmetry of any particular force law and carries no empirical content.

pthm-cm08-point-noether:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]], and let $(\tau,\xi,B)$ be a
symmetry datum of the model's mechanical Lagrangian with $\tau\equiv0$
([[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]] clause (a)); write

$$C(t,x,v):=\bigl(\mathsf M v\bigr)\cdot\xi(t,x)-B(t,x)\qquad\bigl((t,x,v)\in O\bigr)$$

for its charge. Then:

1. **(conservation in the global potential model).** If $d\equiv0$ and $\xi$
   is independent of $t$, then for every motion $x:J\to Q$ of the model on an
   interval $J$ with nonempty interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]), the
   function $t\mapsto C\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)$ is constant on $J$.

2. **(residual-force rate).** For an arbitrary presentation $(U,d)$, along
   every motion $x:J\to Q$ the function $t\mapsto C(t,x(t),x'(t))$ is of class
   $C^{1}$ on $J$ and

$$C'(t)=\bigl\langle d\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr),\,\xi\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\bigr\rangle\qquad(t\in J),$$

   where the pairing is the Euclidean inner product of $\mathbb R^{3N}$;
   consequently $C$ is constant on $J$ if and only if this pairing vanishes
   for every $t\in J$.

Clause 1 is the conditional conservation law of the model's global potential
branch under a symmetry identity of its Lagrangian; clause 2 quantifies the
exact rate at which a residual force destroys it. Neither clause asserts that
any model possesses a strict symmetry datum, and neither carries empirical
content.

pthm-cm08-general-noether.physical_scope: The general point Noether theorem of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: for a symmetry datum with time reparametrisation, the charge M x' . xi - (K+U) tau - B is constant along every motion of the global potential branch; the charge has derivative equal to the residual force paired with xi - x' tau for an arbitrary presentation; the tau=0 and xi=0, tau=1 specialisations reduce to the strict point-symmetry charge and to minus the mechanical energy; and replacing the potential representative U by U+c(t) with the boundary function B-c tau preserves the identity and leaves the charge unchanged. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared presentation and the symmetry identity; it asserts no symmetry of any particular force law, no converse from conservation to symmetry, and carries no empirical content.

pthm-cm08-general-noether:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]], and let $(\tau,\xi,B)$ be a
symmetry datum of the model's mechanical Lagrangian
([[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]] clause (a)), with charge

$$C(t,x,v):=\bigl(\mathsf M v\bigr)\cdot\xi(t,x)-\bigl(K(v)+U(t,x)\bigr)\tau(t,x)-B(t,x)\qquad\bigl((t,x,v)\in O\bigr).$$

Then:

1. **(conservation in the global potential model).** If $d\equiv0$, then for
   every motion $x:J\to Q$ of the model on an interval $J$ with nonempty
   interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]), the function
   $t\mapsto C\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)$ is constant on $J$.

2. **(specialisations).** At $\tau\equiv0$ the model identity is the strict
   identity of clause (b) of [[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]]
   and the charge reduces to $(\mathsf M v)\cdot\xi-B$; at $\xi\equiv0$,
   $\tau\equiv1$, $B\equiv0$ the model identity holds on $O$ if and only if
   $\partial_{t}U\equiv0$ on $I_{0}\times Q$, and the charge is $-E$, where
   $E=K+U$ is the model's mechanical energy function.

3. **(residual-force rate).** For an arbitrary presentation $(U,d)$, along
   every motion $x:J\to Q$ the function $t\mapsto C(t,x(t),x'(t))$ is of class
   $C^{1}$ on $J$ and

$$C'(t)=\Bigl\langle d\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr),\,\xi\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)-x'(t)\,\tau\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\Bigr\rangle\qquad(t\in J);$$

   consequently $C$ is constant on $J$ if and only if this pairing vanishes
   for every $t\in J$.

4. **(potential gauge).** Let $c:I_{0}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{2}$ and let
   $U':=U+c$ be the representative of
   [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (c), with Lagrangian
   $L'=K-U'$; put $B':=B-c\tau$. Then $(\tau,\xi,B')$ is a symmetry datum of
   the model's mechanical Lagrangian for the representative $U'$ if and only
   if $(\tau,\xi,B)$ is one for $U$, and its charge is the same function $C$.
   In particular the conserved quantity of clause 1 does not depend on the
   choice of potential representative, although the mechanical energy
   $E=K+U$ does.

All clauses are conditional deductions from the adopted force branch, the
declared presentation and the stated symmetry identity; no clause asserts that
a given model admits a symmetry datum, and no clause carries empirical content.

pthm-cm08-time-energy.physical_scope: Time translation as a symmetry datum of the force model with a declared potential presentation: the datum (tau,xi,B)=(1,0,0) satisfies the model's Noether identity exactly when the potential has no explicit time dependence; in the global potential branch with an autonomous potential the mechanical energy K+U is constant along every motion; and if the potential depends explicitly on time at a state, then the maximal motion through that state has nonvanishing energy derivative there, so the energy is not conserved. The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch and the declared presentation; the sharpness clause uses the maximal-motion existence theorem, and no empirical content is asserted.

pthm-cm08-time-energy:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]], and let

$$E(t,x,v):=K(v)+U(t,x)=\frac12\,v\cdot\mathsf M v+U(t,x)$$

be the model's mechanical energy function. Consider the datum
$\tau\equiv1$, $\xi\equiv0$, $B\equiv0$ of
[[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]]. Then:

1. **(the identity).** The datum satisfies the model's Noether identity on
   $O$ if and only if $\partial_{t}U\equiv0$ on $I_{0}\times Q$; its charge is
   the function $-E$.
2. **(conservation).** If $d\equiv0$ and $\partial_{t}U\equiv0$, then for
   every motion $x:J\to Q$ of the model on an interval $J$ with nonempty
   interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]), the function
   $t\mapsto E\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)=K(x'(t))+U(t,x(t))$ is constant on $J$.
3. **(sharpness).** If $d\equiv0$ and there is a state $(t_{0},x_{0})\in I_{0}\times Q$
   with $\partial_{t}U(t_{0},x_{0})\ne0$, then the maximal motion
   $x_{\max}:J_{\max}\to Q$ of the model through the initial datum
   $(t_{0},x_{0},0)$ satisfies
   $\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(K(x_{\max}')+U(\cdot,x_{\max})\bigr)|_{t_{0}}=\partial_{t}U(t_{0},x_{0})\ne0$,
   and the mechanical energy is not constant on $J_{\max}$.

The conservation clause is the energy case of the model's Noether identity and
is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared representative $U$ and
the absence of residual forces; the sharpness clause shows that explicit time
dependence of the declared representative destroys conservation along an actual
motion. No empirical content is asserted.

pthm-cm08-translation.physical_scope: Translation symmetry of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: the exact equivalence between the differential invariance condition sum_i a . grad_i U = 0 and finite invariance on admissible translation segments, with the exact component compatibility criterion for all admissible endpoints, the resulting strict symmetry datum and conservation of the component a . P of the total momentum along every motion of the global potential branch, the sharpness statement that a nonzero directional derivative at a state produces a motion whose momentum component is not constant, and the vector form for a fully translation-invariant potential. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared potential and the absence of residual forces in the conservation clauses; it asserts no translation symmetry of any particular force law and carries no empirical content.

pthm-cm08-translation:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]. Fix a nonzero vector
$a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and let $\xi^{a}\in\mathbb R^{3N}$ be the configuration
vector whose $i$-th three-dimensional block is $\xi^{a}_{i}:=a$, so that
$(\mathsf M v)\cdot\xi^{a}=\sum_{i}m_{i}\,a\cdot v_{i}$ for a
velocity $v$. Write $P(t):=\sum_{i}m_{i}x_{i}'(t)$ for the total momentum of
[[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]]. Then:

1. **(infinitesimal and finite invariance).** The following are equivalent:
   (i) $\sum_{i=1}^N a\cdot\nabla_{x_i}U(t,x)=0$ for every
   $(t,x)\in I_0\times Q$; (ii) $U(t,x+s\xi^a)=U(t,x)$ whenever
   the whole segment $\{x+r\xi^a:r\text{ between }0\text{ and }s\}$
   lies in $Q$. More generally, for fixed $(t,x)$ put
   $J_x:=\{s\in\mathbb R:x+s\xi^a\in Q\}$, an open set containing $0$.
   Its interval components are its maximal open intervals. Under (i),
   $s\mapsto U(t,x+s\xi^a)$ is constant on each interval component.
   Invariance for every $s\in J_x$, including components separated by an
   excluded segment, holds if and only if all these component constants
   equal $U(t,x)$. This agreement is automatic when $J_x$ is connected,
   in particular when the whole translation line lies in $Q$.

2. **(the symmetry datum).** Under these equivalent hypotheses the strict
   datum $\tau\equiv0$, $\xi\equiv\xi^{a}$, $B\equiv0$ satisfies the model's
   Noether identity on $O$ in the sense of
   [[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]].

3. **(conservation of the momentum component).** If in addition $d\equiv0$,
   then for every motion $x:J\to Q$ of the model on an interval $J$ with
   nonempty interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]), the function
   $t\mapsto a\cdot P(t)=\sum_{i}\bigl\langle a,\,m_{i}x_{i}'(t)\bigr\rangle$
   is constant on $J$.

4. **(sharpness).** If $d\equiv0$ and there is a state
   $(t_{0},x_{0})\in I_{0}\times Q$ with
   $g:=\sum_{i}a\cdot\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t_{0},x_{0})\ne0$, then the maximal motion
   $x_{\max}:J_{\max}\to Q$ through the initial datum $(t_{0},x_{0},0)$
   satisfies $\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(a\cdot P(t)\bigr)|_{t_{0}}=-g\ne0$; in
   particular $a\cdot P$ is not constant on $J_{\max}$.

5. **(vector form).** If $\sum_{i}\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)=0$ for every
   $(t,x)\in I_{0}\times Q$, then with $d\equiv0$ the total momentum vector
   $P$ is constant along every motion.

The hypotheses are conditions on the declared potential; the conservation
clauses are conditional deductions of the global potential branch, the
sharpness clause locates the failure at an actual motion, and no symmetry of
any particular force law and no empirical content is asserted.

pthm-cm08-rotation.physical_scope: Rotation symmetry of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: the equivalence between the differential invariance condition of the potential along the rotation family with axis a and finite invariance on admissible rotation arcs, with the exact component compatibility criterion for all admissible endpoints, the resulting strict symmetry datum, conservation of the component a . J of the total angular momentum about the inertial origin along every motion of the global potential branch, its sharpness under a nonzero rotational derivative of U, and the vector form when the potential is invariant under all rotations about the origin. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared potential and the absence of residual forces in the conservation clauses; it asserts no rotation symmetry of any particular force law and carries no empirical content.

pthm-cm08-rotation:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]. Fix a nonzero vector
$a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and put, for $s\in\mathbb R$ and $z\in\mathbb R^{3}$,

$$R_{a}(s)z:=z+\frac{\sin\bigl(\lvert a\rvert s\bigr)}{\lvert a\rvert}\,a\times z+\frac{1-\cos\bigl(\lvert a\rvert s\bigr)}{\lvert a\rvert^{2}}\,a\times(a\times z),$$

where $\times$ is the cross product of $\mathbb R^{3}$
([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). For a configuration $x=(x_{1},\dots,x_{N})$
write $R_{a}(s)x:=(R_{a}(s)x_{1},\dots,R_{a}(s)x_{N})$, and let
$\xi^{a}:Q\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ be the vector field with $\xi^{a}_{i}(x):=a\times x_{i}$.
Write $J(t):=\sum_{i}x_{i}(t)\times m_{i}x_{i}'(t)$ for the total angular
momentum about the inertial origin ([[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]]).
Then:

1. **(infinitesimal and finite invariance).** The following are equivalent:
   (i) $\sum_i\langle a\times x_i,\nabla_{x_i}U(t,x)\rangle=0$
   for every $(t,x)\in I_0\times Q$; (ii) $U(t,R_a(s)x)=U(t,x)$
   whenever $\{R_a(r)x:r\text{ between }0\text{ and }s\}$ lies in $Q$.
   More generally put $D_x:=\{s\in\mathbb R:R_a(s)x\in Q\}$, an open set
   containing $0$, with interval components its maximal open intervals.
   Under (i), $s\mapsto U(t,R_a(s)x)$ is constant on each interval
   component. Invariance for every $s\in D_x$, including components
   separated by an excluded arc, holds if and only if all these constants
   equal $U(t,x)$. This agreement is automatic if $D_x$ is connected,
   in particular if the whole rotation orbit is contained in $Q$.

2. **(the symmetry datum).** Under these equivalent hypotheses the strict
   datum $\tau\equiv0$, $\xi\equiv\xi^{a}$, $B\equiv0$ satisfies the model's
   Noether identity on $O$ in the sense of
   [[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]].

3. **(conservation of the angular-momentum component).** If in addition
   $d\equiv0$, then for every motion $x:J\to Q$ of the model on an interval
   $J$ with nonempty interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]), the function
   $t\mapsto a\cdot J(t)=\sum_{i}\bigl\langle a,\,x_{i}(t)\times m_{i}x_{i}'(t)\bigr\rangle$
   is constant on $J$.

4. **(sharpness).** If $d\equiv0$ and there is a state
   $(t_{0},x_{0})\in I_{0}\times Q$ with
   $g:=\sum_{i}\bigl\langle a\times x_{0,i},\,\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t_{0},x_{0})\bigr\rangle\ne0$,
   then the maximal motion $x_{\max}:J_{\max}\to Q$ through the initial datum
   $(t_{0},x_{0},0)$ satisfies
   $\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(a\cdot J(t)\bigr)|_{t_{0}}=-g\ne0$; in particular
   $a\cdot J$ is not constant on $J_{\max}$.

5. **(vector form).** If $\sum_{i}x_{i}\times\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)=0$ for every
   $(t,x)\in I_{0}\times Q$, then with $d\equiv0$ the total angular momentum
   vector $J$ is constant along every motion.

The hypothesis is a condition on the declared potential — equivalently, by
clause 1, invariance of $U$ along admissible arcs of the simultaneous rotations
$R_a(s)$ of all labels, with full endpoint invariance requiring the component
agreement specified there; the conservation clauses are conditional deductions of the global
potential branch, and no symmetry of any particular force law and no empirical
content is asserted.

pthm-cm08-boost-boundary.physical_scope: The Galilean boost charge of the force model with a declared potential presentation in one inertial frame: the time-dependent symmetry datum (tau, xi, B) = (0, t a, a . M x) satisfies the model's Noether identity exactly when the potential is invariant under the simultaneous translation of all labels by the vector a; in the global potential branch the boost charge a . (t P - M X) is then constant, the component a of the centre of mass moves uniformly, and the boosted curves t -> x(t) + s t a of motions are again motions; for an arbitrary presentation the exact rate of the charge is the time times the component a of the total force, and a nonzero translation derivative of the potential at a nonzero time produces a motion along which the charge is not constant. The theorem is conditional on the adopted force branch, the declared potential and the absence of residual forces in the conservation clauses; it asserts no boost invariance of any particular force law and carries no empirical content.

pthm-cm08-boost-boundary:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]. Fix a nonzero vector
$a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and consider the maps

$$\xi^{a}(t,x):=t\,\bigl(a,\dots,a\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{3N},\qquad B^{a}(t,x):=\bigl\langle a,\mathsf M x\bigr\rangle=\sum_{i}m_{i}\,a\cdot x_{i},$$

so that $(\tau,\xi,B)\equiv(0,\xi^{a},B^{a})$ is a datum of
[[def-cm08-symmetry-of-the-mechanical-lagrangian]]. Write
$P(t):=\sum_{i}m_{i}x_{i}'(t)$ for the total momentum and $X$ for the centre
of mass of [[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]], with
$\mathsf M X=\sum_{i}m_{i}x_{i}$, and define the **boost charge**

$$K_{a}(t):=a\cdot\bigl(t\,P(t)-\mathsf M X(t)\bigr)=t\,\bigl(a\cdot P(t)\bigr)-\sum_{i}m_{i}\,a\cdot x_{i}(t).$$

Then:

1. **(the identity).** The datum $(0,\xi^{a},B^{a})$ satisfies the model's
   Noether identity on $O$ if and only if the translation-invariance condition
   $\sum_{i}a\cdot\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)=0$ for all $(t,x)\in I_{0}\times Q$
   of clause 1 of [[pthm-cm08-translation]] holds.
2. **(conservation).** If in addition $d\equiv0$, then for every motion
   $x:J\to Q$ of the model on an interval $J$ with nonempty interior
   ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]), the function $t\mapsto K_{a}(t)$ is constant
   on $J$.
3. **(uniform centre-of-mass motion).** Under the hypotheses of clause 2, the
   function $t\mapsto a\cdot\mathsf M X(t)$ is affine on $J$ with slope
   $a\cdot P$.
4. **(boosted motions).** Under the hypotheses of clause 2, let $x:J\to Q$
   be a motion and $s\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $x(t)+st\xi^a_1\in Q$ for every
   $t\in J$, where $\xi^a_1=(a,\dots,a)$. Then
   $\widetilde x(t):=x(t)+st\xi^a_1$ is a motion if and only if
   $\nabla_xU(t,\widetilde x(t))=\nabla_xU(t,x(t))$ for every $t\in J$.
   This equality, and hence the boosted-motion conclusion, follows if
   each segment between $x(t)$ and $\widetilde x(t)$ is contained in $Q$,
   or if the all-admissible-endpoint finite invariance criterion of
   [[pthm-cm08-translation]] clause 1 holds.

5. **(the general rate and the boundary).** For an arbitrary presentation
   $(U,d)$ and every motion $x:J\to Q$,

$$K_{a}'(t)=t\,a\cdot F_{\mathrm{tot}}(t),\qquad F_{\mathrm{tot}}(t):=\sum_{i}F_{i}\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr);$$

   consequently, when $d\equiv0$, the charge $K_{a}$ is constant on $J$ if and
   only if $t\mapsto t\sum_{i}a\cdot\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x(t))$ vanishes
   identically on $J$, and if the translation-invariance condition fails at
   some state, then there are a time $t_{0}\ne0$ and a state $x_{0}$ with
   $g:=\sum_{i}a\cdot\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t_{0},x_{0})\ne0$ such that the maximal
   motion through $(t_{0},x_{0},0)$ satisfies $K_{a}'(t_{0})=-t_{0}\,g\ne0$
   and $K_{a}$ is not constant on its interval.

The charge exists as a conserved quantity exactly under the same potential
invariance that conserves the momentum component $a\cdot P$; the conservation
clauses are conditional deductions of the global potential branch, and no
empirical content is asserted.

pthm-cm08-moving-chart-energy-function.physical_scope: The energy bookkeeping of a time-dependent coordinate description of the force model: for a C^3 coordinate map X with everywhere invertible configuration Jacobian and the substituted Lagrangian of the covariance theorem, the chart energy function equals the inertial mechanical energy plus or minus the pairing of the chart's explicit time dependence with the mass-operator velocity, so the two agree exactly when that pairing vanishes; the chart energy function is conserved along chart Euler-Lagrange solutions whenever the substituted Lagrangian has no explicit time dependence along the trajectory; and in the global potential branch the chart description of every motion solves that chart equation. The statement concerns the model's coordinate description, is conditional on the adopted force branch and the declared presentation, and asserts no measurement and no identification of the chart energy with the inertial mechanical energy.

pthm-cm08-moving-chart-energy-function:
## Statement

Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $U$ of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3N}$
be open and nonempty and let $X:\Omega\to Q$ be of class $C^{3}$ with
$X_{q}(t,q)$ invertible for every $(t,q)\in\Omega$; let

$$\widetilde O:=\bigl\{(t,q,v)\in\Omega\times\mathbb R^{3N}:\bigl(t,X(t,q),X_{t}(t,q)+X_{q}(t,q)v\bigr)\in O\bigr\},\qquad \widetilde L(t,q,v):=L\bigl(t,X(t,q),\,X_{t}(t,q)+X_{q}(t,q)v\bigr)$$

be the substituted data of [[pthm-cm07-coordinate-covariance-of-the-equations]].
Let $q:J\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ be a $C^{2}$ curve with
$(t,q(t),q'(t))\in\widetilde O$ for every $t\in J$, and put $x(t):=X(t,q(t))$.
Define the **chart energy function** and the **inertial mechanical energy**
along the curve by

$$e(t):=q'(t)\cdot\widetilde L_{v}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)-\widetilde L\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr),\qquad E_{\mathrm{in}}(t):=K\bigl(x'(t)\bigr)+U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr).$$

Then:

1. **(difference identity).** For every $t\in J$,

$$E_{\mathrm{in}}(t)=e(t)+\bigl\langle X_{t}\bigl(t,q(t)\bigr),\,\mathsf M x'(t)\bigr\rangle;$$

   equivalently
   $e(t)=\tfrac12\langle X_{q}v,\mathsf M X_{q}v\rangle-\tfrac12\langle X_{t},\mathsf M X_{t}\rangle+U(t,X)$
   at $(t,q(t),q'(t))$.
2. **(coincidence criterion).** $e(t)=E_{\mathrm{in}}(t)$ if and only if
   $\langle X_{t}(t,q(t)),\mathsf M x'(t)\rangle=0$; in particular
   $e=E_{\mathrm{in}}$ along the curve whenever $X_{t}(t,q(t))=0$.
3. **(conservation of the chart energy).** If
   $\widetilde L_{t}(t,q(t),q'(t))=0$ for every $t\in J$ and $q$ solves the
   chart Euler-Lagrange equation $E_{\widetilde L}(q)=0$ on $J$, then $e$ is
   constant on $J$; this includes in particular the case
   $\widetilde L_{t}\equiv0$ on $\widetilde O$.
4. **(model motions in the global potential branch).** If $d\equiv0$ and
   $x:J\to Q$ is a motion of the model with $q$ its chart description, then
   $E_{\widetilde L}(q)=0$ on $J$.

The difference identity and the coincidence criterion hold for every
presentation; clauses 3 and 4 are the conservation statement of the moving
description and its link to the model's motions. No identification of the
chart energy function with the inertial mechanical energy is asserted, and no
empirical content is claimed.

rem-cm08-external-symmetry-breaking.physical_scope: Scope audit of the symmetry and conservation statements of the pair: the symmetry criteria are conditions on the model's declared Lagrangian and potential, not on the kinematic framework; force laws with external or confining potentials break the corresponding charges, with the failure rates computed by the sharpness clauses; residual forces destroy conservation of a symmetry charge unless they pair to zero with the generator along the motion; in a moving coordinate description the conserved chart energy function need not be the inertial mechanical energy; time-dependent potentials break energy conservation; and no converse from an observed conservation to a symmetry of a model, and no empirical claim, is asserted. The remark adds no new physical claim.

ex-cm08-uniform-field-breaks-translation.physical_scope: A worked model check inside the framework: the one-label uniform-force model with its potential presentation U = -m g . x, its explicit maximal motion, the failure of the translation and boost charges in directions with a nonzero component along the field, with the exact rates predicted by the sharpness clauses, a numerical instance at an explicit time, and the survival of the mechanical energy because the potential has no explicit time dependence. All values are model values in a declared idealization; the example reports no measurement and asserts no property of any field of nature.

ex-cm08-pair-potential-charges-check.physical_scope: A worked check of the conservation statements of the pair on a two-label pair-potential model: for a potential depending on the labels through a C^2 function of the squared separation, the pair force is antisymmetric and central; the translation condition of the momentum theorem and the rotation condition of the angular-momentum theorem hold identically for every field direction and axis; the momentum, angular-momentum, boost and energy charges are therefore conserved along every motion of this model class; and an explicit rigid-rotation motion with a Hooke-type pair potential is verified together with its charges and a numerical instance. All values are model values of the declared idealization; the example reports no measurement and asserts no property of any physical interaction.

ex-cm08-rotating-chart-hamiltonian-not-m.physical_scope: A worked computation of the moving-chart energy bookkeeping on an explicit model: the one-label isotropic oscillator with potential U = k |x|^2 / 2, observed in a chart rotating uniformly about the third axis; the substituted Lagrangian, its Legendre data and its Hamiltonian are computed, the difference identity between the chart Hamiltonian and the inertial mechanical energy is verified as the pairing of the chart's angular velocity with the momentum, an explicit circular motion with k = m omega^2 is shown to have chart Hamiltonian zero and inertial mechanical energy m omega^2 r^2, and a numerical instance is evaluated. All values are model values of the declared idealization; the example reports no measurement and asserts no property of an apparatus.

ex-cm08-time-dependent-potential-breaks-.physical_scope: A worked model check inside the framework: a one-label model in the three-dimensional force branch whose potential depends explicitly on time through a prescribed vector drive f(t), with force -k x + f(t); the time-translation identity of the pair holds exactly when the drive is constant, the mechanical energy changes at the rate -f'(t) . x along motions, and for the sinusoidally driven specialisation an explicit global motion is exhibited whose energy derivative at a stated time is nonzero, together with a numerical instance. All values are model values of the declared idealization; the drive is adopted external data, and the example reports no measurement.
